sources_considered.why: Full text of Accenture's Q3 FY26 press release (Business Wire copy).

receipt.public_excerpt: Company now expects full-year revenue growth to be 3% to 4% in local currency.

evidence_items.explanation: In June 2026 Accenture expected 3% to 4% growth for FY26, down from 7% in FY25. That is not the AI-driven step-up its September framing suggested.

receipt.public_excerpt: The company reported a 2% decline in new bookings for the quarter ended May 31 and forecast revenue of $17.75 billion to $18.4 billion for the three months through August, below the $18.47 billion expected by Bloomberg-compiled analysts. Accenture shares fell 20% in early New York trading, marking their worst one-day drop on record.

evidence_items.explanation: Bookings fell, the outlook missed analyst estimates, and the stock had its worst day on record. All of this points to AI not yet paying off visibly.

receipt.public_excerpt: Bloomberg Intelligence said weak sales and another soft bookings period reinforce concerns that AI may be disrupting demand across consulting and managed services, while also noting that demand for consultants has been soft partly because the Middle East conflict has hit discretionary spending.

evidence_items.explanation: An outside analyst view that matches the speaker's aside that AI may be hurting demand. It also names the Middle East conflict as a separate cause.

evidence_items.locator: Full Year Fiscal 2025 Financial Review, Fiscal 2025 Revenues

receipt.public_excerpt: Revenues for fiscal 2025 were $69.67 billion, an increase of 7% in both U.S. dollars and local currency.

evidence_items.explanation: The baseline. In September 2025, Accenture's headline said early AI investments helped drive this 7% growth.

receipt.public_excerpt: Revenues of $18.7 billion, an increase of $1.0 billion, 6% in U.S. dollars and 3% in local currency

evidence_items.explanation: Revenue still grew, and the same release reports EPS up 9% and a higher margin. The business was not in decline, which weakens a strong 'did not pay off' reading.

evidence_items.locator: Full Year Fiscal 2026 Financial Review, Fiscal 2026 Revenues

receipt.public_excerpt:
Revenues for fiscal 2026 were $74.18 billion, an increase of 6% in U.S. dollars and 5% in local currency, and

evidence_items.explanation: After the post, FY26 finished at 5% growth, above the June guidance. This is outside the target period, so it is context only, but it tempers the picture.

unresolved_gaps: In FY26 Accenture stopped reporting separate AI bookings and revenue figures, so AI-specific returns cannot be isolated.
Accenture blamed part of the Q3 shortfall on the Middle East conflict and on deals that slipped, not on AI.
